app/artifacts.html:
Using Vythea/The app

Artifacts and previews

The files Vythea makes for you, and previewing pages and pictures.

When you ask for a page, a chart or a small app, Vythea first makes it as one file you can preview. It moves to a project on your computer only when the work needs one, and to Vythea Cloud only when your computer cannot do it, and then with your yes.

The Artifacts page

In the window, Artifacts lists the files Vythea writes, newest first. For each one:

  • Preview shows it in the window. HTML and SVG files are drawn as pages.
  • Show in folder opens the folder it is in.
  • Open in your browser opens it in your own browser, on this computer only.

Previews open by themselves when a file is made, unless you turn that off.

Previewing from the terminal

/preview serves an HTML or SVG file to your browser. --open opens it at once.

/preview --open chart.html

Files a turn changed

At the end of a turn, the window lists the files it changed. The Changes tab beside the chat shows every edit of the session: review or revert them, then stage, commit and push. The Files tab browses and previews the project. In the terminal, /diff shows what changed in the project, and /diff session only this session's files.

Pictures, speech and video

What Vythea makes with hosted models is saved in media/ in the project folder, or in your data folder when no project is attached. Pictures open in the window's own viewer.

app/helpers.title: Helpers and workflows
app/helpers.description: Vythea handing parts of a task to helpers, running workflows of many helpers, and working in a git worktree.
app/helpers.html:
Using Vythea/The app

Helpers and workflows

Vythea handing parts of a task to helpers, running workflows of many helpers, and working in a git worktree.

Helpers

On a bigger task, Vythea can hand parts of the work to helpers: other agents that work side by side for the session.

  • They share the session's task list, with who owns each item and what blocks it.
  • They go through the same approvals as the session, in its mode and with its rules.
  • They share one token budget across all of them.
  • A helper can work in a git worktree of its own, so it does not touch your checkout.
  • A kept helper waits for more work and wakes when it gets a message.

To see them at work:

  • In the window, open Activity: what each helper is doing, with a way to read, steer or stop it. Its approvals come to you as usual.
  • In the terminal, /agents lists the helpers working for this session; stop one or tell it something.

Helpers' conversations are kept beside their session, out of the session list.

Workflows

A workflow is a script that runs many helpers for a big task. Vythea can write one and run it once you approve it: the card shows the script first.

  • /crew lets Vythea run workflows of helpers for big tasks. Start a message with @crew to allow it for that message alone.
  • /workflows lists workflow runs: look in, pause, stop, resume, skip or retry them. In the window, the Workflows page does the same, and shows one helper's conversation or a run's log.
  • A finished part of a run is not done again when the run is resumed.
  • A saved workflow runs as a slash command. /review, which looks over a change, comes built in.

Working in a worktree

To start a terminal session in a git worktree of its own, on a new branch made from where you are, leaving your checkout alone:

vythea --worktree

When it is done, its work can be applied back.

app/memory.title: Memory
app/memory.description: What Vythea remembers between sessions, when it saves, where it keeps it, and how to see and change it.
app/memory.html:
Using Vythea/The app

Memory

What Vythea remembers between sessions, when it saves, where it keeps it, and how to see and change it.

Vythea keeps notes between sessions in plain files on your computer. You can read and change all of them.

What it keeps

MemoryHolds
About you (USER.md)what Vythea knows about you
Its notes (MEMORY.md)its own notes, for every chat
Projectnotes on one project, kept in your data folder, never in the repository
This chatnotes for one chat alone; they go when the chat is deleted
Soul (SOUL.md)who Vythea is, in your words; optional

Once SOUL.md has something in it, it takes the place of Vythea's own first line in every request. A project's AGENTS.md is read as that project's instructions; see Project instructions.

Memory refuses keys and passwords, and text that tries to give Vythea orders.

When it saves

By default, Vythea saves to memory only when you ask. You can choose, for each chat or for all of them:

ChoiceSaves
when askedonly when you ask it to remember something
askwhen it thinks something is worth keeping, after your yes
autoon its own

While it saves on its own, it can also look back every 10 messages for what to remember; /memory-review turns that on or off.

Where it keeps it

ChoiceKeeps memory
autoeverywhere: about you, its notes, the project and the chat
projectfor this project
chatfor this chat only

With no project folder attached, "project" means the chat's own notes.

Choosing in the terminal

/remember shows and changes when this chat saves and where. Followed by text, it keeps that text:

/remember I prefer tabs to spaces
/remember --project the tests need Docker running
/remember --chat call the draft v2

To start the terminal with a choice:

vythea --memory auto --memory-scope project

--memory takes when-asked, ask or auto; --memory-scope takes auto, project or chat.

Private chats

A private chat loads only its own notes and saves to them only when asked. Nothing typed in it is kept in the terminal's prompt history.

vythea --private

Seeing and changing it

  • In the window, open Settings > Memory. Each entry can be edited or deleted, and SOUL.md can be written there.
  • In the terminal, /memory shows what is kept. /memory edit opens a file in your editor, /memory log lists the changes, and /memory restore puts an earlier version back. Each takes user, memory, project or soul:
/memory edit user
/memory log project

You can also open the files in your data folder and edit them yourself.

app.description: The Vythea window: sessions, models, settings, and what differs on Windows, Linux and macOS.
app.html:
Using Vythea

The app

The Vythea window: sessions, models, settings, and what differs on Windows, Linux and macOS.

The window is a chat with an agent in it. Sessions are listed on the left, with search, pinning and date groups; each session is its own file on your disk, so two copies of Vythea can run at once.

Talking to it

  • Replies stream in as markdown. Tools the agent uses — reading files, running commands, reading a web page, searching past sessions — show in the chat, and anything that changes your computer asks first.
  • Pick the model from the model menu. It lists every model from Vythea and from each gateway you have set up, and a message goes to the gateway of the model you pick.
  • Effort, thinking and web search can be switched where the model supports them.
  • When a conversation outgrows the model's window, older turns are summarised instead of forgotten.

Ctrl+K opens a palette of actions, pages, sessions and models, and every part of the window can be reached from the keyboard. Beside the chat, the Files tab browses the project, the Changes tab reviews and reverts this session's edits, and the Jobs tab shows background commands.

Settings

  • Accounts: each gateway, where it stands — signed in, connected, not set up, not running — and its key.
  • Account: who is signed in, your credit, and who pays for hosted models: you, or a team you are in.
  • The other pages hold the rest, among them Search (the search service), Model (a cheaper side model for summaries, and session names), Appearance (colours and film grain), Memory and Wallet.

The window can also be reached from Telegram and Discord, and scheduled jobs report there. Artifacts and Skills have their own pages.

Closing the window keeps Vythea in the tray on Windows and Linux: click the icon to bring it back, or right-click to quit. Uninstall from Apps & features on Windows, or with vythea --uninstall.

app/permissions.title: Asking first and modes
app/permissions.description: When Vythea asks before it acts, the six modes, plan mode, and what is refused in every mode.
app/permissions.html:
Using Vythea/The app

Asking first and modes

When Vythea asks before it acts, the six modes, plan mode, and what is refused in every mode.

Vythea reads and searches on its own. Anything that changes your computer, such as writing a file or running a command, asks first: a card shows what it wants to do, and you allow or deny it. In the window, Enter allows and Escape denies. When one reply asks about several calls, the card says "2 of 3".

The modes

The mode decides how much runs without asking. Each session keeps its own.

ModeName in commandsWhat runs without asking
Askdefaultnothing that writes or runs; every change asks
Editsaccept-editsedits inside the project; commands still ask
Planplanreading and searching only; nothing is written or run
Autoautoedits inside the project; your own model judges the rest
Don't askdont-askonly what you allowed before; whatever would ask is refused
Bypassbypasseverything, except risky calls and your own rules

Change it with the mode switch in the window, or in the terminal:

/mode accept-edits

In the terminal, Shift+Tab (or Alt+M) steps through Ask, Edits, Plan and Auto, and Bypass once you have chosen it. The footer says for a moment what each mode lets run. To start the terminal in a mode:

vythea --mode auto

--plan is the same as --mode plan, and --yes the same as --mode bypass. Use Bypass only where that is safe.

Plan mode

Plan mode is for thinking before doing. Vythea reads, searches and makes a plan, and refuses any tool that would change something, however it is asked for. Turn it on and off with /plan; turning it off goes back to the mode you were in.

Auto mode

In Auto, a judge running on your own model decides each call that would otherwise ask. Each call it let through or blocked is listed: /decisions in the terminal, or the Decisions list in the window. Auto allows installs inside the project and local git, but not a push nobody asked for.

On macOS and Linux, a command in Edits or Auto can also run confined by the system instead of asking: no network, and writes only inside the project.

Allowed for this session

When you allow a call, you can allow it for the rest of the session too. Approvals given in one session stay in that session.

Refused in every mode

Some things are refused whatever the mode:

  • Catastrophic commands, such as deleting your home folder.
  • A command that uploads a key file, with curl, wget, scp or rsync.
  • Reading secret files, such as .env and private keys. .env.example is fine.

After Vythea has read text from outside, such as a web page, risky calls are checked again even in Bypass.

Switching tools off

Any tool can be switched off, in Capabilities > Tools in the window. A tool that cannot work on your computer is not offered.

app/scheduled-jobs.title: Scheduled jobs and loops
app/scheduled-jobs.description: Prompts that run on a timer, sessions that keep working toward a goal, and being told when a run ends.
app/scheduled-jobs.html:
Using Vythea/The app

Scheduled jobs and loops

Prompts that run on a timer, sessions that keep working toward a goal, and being told when a run ends.

Scheduled jobs

A scheduled job sends a prompt at a time you set. Each run opens a session of its own.

  1. In the window, open Scheduled jobs and choose New job.
  2. Give it a name and the prompt to send.
  3. Pick when: at a time of day (weekdays only, if you like), or on an interval.
  4. Pick the mode it runs in. Plan reads and searches only: nothing is written or run. See Asking first and modes.
  5. Save it. Run now runs it straight away.

You can also ask in the chat: "every morning at 9, check the deploy and tell me if it failed". Vythea can add, list and remove jobs, and asks you first. A job can also run once, at a date and time, and can stay quiet unless something changed.

Jobs run in whichever copy of Vythea is open, the window or the terminal, never twice. They keep working while the window is hidden in the tray. To run them with no window open, use:

vythea serve

A job can report to a chat app: switch on Report scheduled jobs here on the Messaging page. See Telegram, Discord and Slack.

Loops in one session

/loop sends a prompt again and again in this session: every so often, or at the model's own pace.

/loop 10m check CI
/loop stop

/heartbeat looks in on this session every so many minutes:

/heartbeat 30 check the deploy

Working toward a goal

/goal keeps a session working until a goal is met: after each turn, a quick check decides whether to carry on. /goal --check adds a command to the goal; while that command fails, the goal is not met.

/goal all tests pass
/goal --check cargo test
/goal clear

/goal alone shows the goal. A goal that is blocked gets one more try, then pauses, as it does after twenty turns in a row; /goal resume carries on.

Being told when it is done

/notify tells you when a reply ends or needs you while you are away. Turn it off with /notify off.

In the background

In the window, /bg followed by a prompt runs it in the background, beside the chat. Commands still running at their time limit carry on as background jobs: /jobs lists them, and the Jobs tab shows them in the window.

app/sessions.title: Sessions
app/sessions.description: Finding, resuming, rewinding, branching, summarising and exporting conversations.
app/sessions.html:
Using Vythea/The app

Sessions

Finding, resuming, rewinding, branching, summarising and exporting conversations.

Each conversation is a session, kept as its own file in your data folder. The window and the terminal share them: start one in the window and carry on in the terminal.

Finding a session

  • In the window, sessions are listed on the left, with pinning, date groups and filters. Search finds words in any order. Ctrl+Tab switches between recent sessions, and Ctrl+K opens a palette that finds sessions too.
  • In the terminal, /resume lists the recent sessions; a word after it finds one by its title or by what was said.
vythea --continue
vythea --resume

The first picks up this folder's most recent session; the second lets you choose. /where shows the session's file.

Names

A session is named by a model once its first reply is in. A name you give it yourself is never replaced.

  • In the terminal, /rename names it, or with nothing after it asks for a new name now. /model names picks the model that names sessions, or turns naming off.
  • In the window, Name it again is in a session's menu, and Settings > Model > Session names switches naming off or picks the model.

Going back

  • Rewind: go back to any message you sent. Vythea asks whether to restore the code and the conversation, the conversation alone, or the code alone. In the window, use Rewind to here on a message, or press Escape twice in an empty box. In the terminal, use /rewind (or /undo), or press Esc twice on an empty box.
  • Retry: /retry asks your last message again.
  • Branch: /branch carries on in a copy of the session, leaving the first as it was. In the window, use Fork from here on a message.

Rewinding also puts back what a command changed in the project.

When a conversation gets long

When a conversation outgrows the model's window, older turns are summarised instead of forgotten. You can summarise now, too:

/compact
/compact 3

The second keeps the last three turns word for word. /context shows what fills the context, part by part. The terminal's box and the window's status bar say how full it is.

Asking aside

/btw asks something aside without derailing the conversation. The answer is not kept.

Exporting and copying

  • /export writes the conversation as Markdown, to a file in the project named after the session, or to the file you name.
  • /copy copies the last reply as written; /copy 2 the one before it.

Bringing in other sessions

Continue a session from Claude Code or Codex, in the window or the terminal:

/import

Deleting old sessions

Sessions are kept until you delete them. To delete those untouched for 30 days:

/retention 30

/retention off keeps them all again.

Usage

/usage adds up tokens and cost for this session, by day and by model. /insights shows the last weeks by day and hour, with the top tools and models.

app/skills.title: Skills and your own commands
app/skills.description: Saved instructions Vythea can follow, and prompts you run as slash commands.
app/skills.html:
Using Vythea/The app

Skills and your own commands

Saved instructions Vythea can follow, and prompts you run as slash commands.

A skill is a set of instructions Vythea can follow when a task needs it, with any files those instructions use. Vythea sees each skill's name and description, and reads the rest only when it uses one.

Where skills come from

  • Built in: a few come with Vythea, including one that explains Vythea's own commands and settings.
  • Yours: in the skills folder of your data folder.
  • The project's: in .agents/skills or .claude/skills in the project folder.
  • Learned: skills the model saves from work that went well. They start switched off until you switch them on.
  • From plugins: see Plugins, hooks and more.

When two skills have the same name, yours wins.

Writing one

A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md in it: frontmatter with its name and description, then the instructions. It is the same layout Claude's skills use, so those work here too.

---
name: release-notes
description: Write release notes from the git log since the last tag.
---

1. Find the last tag with `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`.
2. ...

In the window, open Capabilities and choose New skill to write one there. A built-in skill can be copied with Copy to edit.

Adding and switching skills

In the terminal:

/skills
/skills add owner/repo
/skills on release-notes
/skills off release-notes

/skills lists every skill and uses one; /skills add adds skills from a GitHub repository, a link or a folder. In the window, the same is on the Capabilities page.

Every skill that is switched on also runs as a slash command by its name, such as /release-notes.

Your own commands

A command is a prompt kept in a Markdown file, run as /name. Whatever you type after the name goes into the text. A subfolder makes folder:name.

  • Yours go in the commands folder of your data folder.
  • A project's go in .vythea/commands or .claude/commands.

The files are the same as Claude Code's: name.md, with an optional description and argument-hint in the frontmatter.

When you run a command, its text is put in the box for you to read before you send it. If a project's command has the same name as yours, yours wins.

Saved workflows run as slash commands too, and /review comes built in.

app/tools.title: What the agent can do
app/tools.description: The tools Vythea uses: files, commands, web search, reading documents, attaching pictures and controlling apps.
app/tools.html:
Using Vythea/The app

What the agent can do

The tools Vythea uses: files, commands, web search, reading documents, attaching pictures and controlling apps.

Vythea works through tools. Each one it uses shows in the chat, and anything that changes your computer asks first: see Asking first and modes.

Files

  • It reads, searches, writes and edits files in the project folder, and shows a diff before each change.
  • It reads Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files as text, OpenDocument files, and EPUB books chapter by chapter. Search can look inside documents too.
  • Scratch work, such as a script to reproduce a bug, can go in the system's temp folder, out of your project.
  • With no project folder attached, a chat works in Vythea's own folder.

Commands

  • It runs commands in the project folder, in bash where bash is installed.
  • A command still running at its time limit carries on as a background job. /jobs lists them in the terminal, and the Jobs tab in the window shows them live.
  • In the terminal, a line starting with ! runs as a command yourself, without asking, and the model sees what it printed with your next message:
!git status

Web search and pages

Vythea can read a web page and search the web. Switch search on with the Web switch in the window, or /search in the terminal.

By default, search goes through the gateway when it sells search (on the Vythea gateway, paid from your credit), and through DuckDuckGo when it cannot answer. The approval card says where a search goes and who pays. To use a search service of your own, open Settings > Search, or:

/search services
ServiceNeeds
Brave, Tavily, Exaan API key
SearXNGyour own server
DuckDuckGonothing; it may be slow or limited at busy times

A chosen service is the only one used. To keep every search on DuckDuckGo, with no key and no cost:

/search keyless

Pictures

The model sees pictures you attach and pictures its tools open. In the window, drop or paste them into the box. In the terminal, Ctrl+V attaches the picture on the clipboard, dragging a picture file in attaches it, or:

/image screenshot.png

Files and folders by name

Type @ and a path to attach a file, a range of lines or a folder. The box offers paths as you type.

Controlling apps

On macOS, and on Linux under X11, Vythea can use desktop apps for you. It asks once for each app.

Speaking and listening

  • Replies can be read aloud as they stream, paid from your credit. In the terminal, /voice turns it on or off.
  • In the window, voice input turns what you say into text at the cursor.

Images, speech and video

Making images, speech and video, and turning audio into text, are covered in Hosted models and credit. A picture you attach can also be edited with edit_image, on the chat's own gateway.

Reply style

/style lists the reply styles and picks one; you can also write your own.

/style concise

chat-apps.title: Telegram, Discord and Slack
chat-apps.description: Talking to Vythea from a chat app on your phone, and getting scheduled jobs' reports there.
chat-apps.html:
Connect and extend

Telegram, Discord and Slack

Talking to Vythea from a chat app on your phone, and getting scheduled jobs' reports there.

Vythea can answer you from Telegram, Discord or Slack: send a message, get a reply. Set each one up in the window, on the Messaging page. Keys and tokens are kept on your computer.

In a chat app:

  • Replies come whole and formatted.
  • Files, photos and voice notes go both ways.
  • A call that needs your yes comes with Allow and Deny buttons, once you switch on Let messages use tools. Off, a message can read and search but not write or run anything.
  • Scheduled jobs can report there: switch on Report scheduled jobs here. See Scheduled jobs and loops.

Telegram

  1. On the Messaging page, open Telegram and choose Open @BotFather. Make a bot there and copy the token it gives you.
  2. Paste it as the Bot token, and save.
  3. Choose Pair a chat. A code shows.
  4. Send the code to your bot from the chat it should answer. In a group, mention the bot first. The code works for 10 minutes, and five wrong codes void it.

Only that chat gets answers.

Discord

  1. On the Messaging page, open Discord and choose Open the Developer Portal. Make an application with a bot, and copy the bot's token.
  2. Paste it as the Bot token.
  3. Add your Discord user ID: the only person the bot answers.
  4. Save. Talk to Vythea in a direct message to the bot, or in a server it is in.

A Webhook URL is optional: with one, Vythea can post results to a channel. With only a webhook and no bot, it sends but does not answer.

Slack

  1. On the Messaging page, open Slack and choose Open your Slack apps. Make an app for your workspace.
  2. Paste its App-level token (it starts with xapp-) and its Bot token (it starts with xoxb-).
  3. Choose Pair. Send the code shown to your app as a direct message. Whoever sends it is the one member answered; five wrong codes void it.

Talk to Vythea in a direct message, or mention it in a channel.

With no window open

The chat apps are answered while the window is open, or hidden in the tray. To answer them with no window, for example on a computer that stays on, run:

vythea serve

It also runs your scheduled jobs. When you open the window, it takes over.

While your computer is off

With Vythea Cloud, the cloud can answer your Telegram chat while this computer is off:

vythea cloud relay on

vythea cloud relay off hands it back.

Cloud and teams/Vythea Cloud

What Vythea Cloud costs

How tasks, services and web apps are charged, and where to see what you spent.

Vythea Cloud comes with Pro and is paid from your credit. There are two kinds of charge: the compute, and the models a task uses.

Compute

Compute is about $6 per GB a month, charged by the second for the memory in use.

WhatCharged
A taskby the second it runs, for its size's memory
A terminal in the browserby the second it is open
A serviceby the hour, while it runs
A web appby the second, only while it is awake
A live link to what a task madenothing

Examples, online all month:

ServiceAbout
128 MB$0.75
256 MB$1.50

A stopped service, and a sleeping web app, cost nothing.

Models

The models a task uses are paid as any hosted request, at the prices on the models page, with Pro's lower prices. See Hosted models and credit.

When credit runs out

A service is stopped and a terminal is closed. Add credit and start them again.

Seeing what you spent

  • The Cloud page shows what each service and web app has cost, how long it was billed, and each task with its compute.
  • The usage page lists every Cloud charge, day by day, beside text and media.

Mining, flooding other machines, and anything the terms forbid. Every container is watched: a miner or a flood is stopped at once, and the team is told of anything else that looks wrong.

cloud.html:
Cloud and teams

Vythea Cloud

Run a task on Vythea's servers, keep a service running, or host a web app with its own link, all from the chat.

Vythea Cloud is the same Vythea agent, running on Vythea's servers instead of your computer. A task sent there keeps going when you close the app or the laptop, and what it builds can stay up: a web app gets its own link, and a service can keep running. It comes with Pro and is paid from your credit.

Running a task there

Just ask in the chat, in the window or the terminal: "run this in the cloud", or anything this computer cannot do well, such as a long build. Vythea asks before it sends a task, since it spends credit. The cloud sees nothing of your computer, so the task carries everything it needs, or an https git repository to clone.

  • Each task runs in a container of its own, with the memory and time of its size: light 512 MB for 15 minutes, normal 1 GB for 30, heavy 2 GB for an hour.
  • Its progress shows as it goes, and closing the app does not stop it; only Stop does.
  • A conversation there keeps its folder and its history, so the next message carries on where the last one left off.
  • What it made can be opened from a preview link in its answer.

From the terminal you can also send one straight away: vythea cloud "task", with --repo <url>, --tier light|normal|heavy and --thread <id> to carry on.

Services that stay online

Ask for something that must keep running, such as "watch my shop's stock every hour, email me when anything runs low, and keep it running". A scheduler, a webhook receiver or a chat bot all work the same way. Vythea builds and tests it, then leaves it running as a worker. Only say "keep it running" (or "keep it online") when you want that: anything else runs once and stops.

  • A worker is restarted if it stops, and stopped for good after it crashes five times in ten minutes, saying why.
  • It gets 256 MB unless it needs more (128 to 512 MB), and an account may keep three running.
  • It is billed by the hour from your credit, and stopped if the credit runs out. A 128 MB service online all month costs about $0.75, a 256 MB one about $1.50.
  • Keys it needs, such as an API token, go in /work/.env in its folder, not in its code.

Web apps with a link

A web app Vythea builds there can stay up at its own address, https://lc-<id>.vythea.si. It wakes on the first visit, sleeps after ten minutes without one, and is awake at most eight hours a day. You only pay while it is awake.

Looking after them

The Cloud page lists what you host, with what each printed last, Stop, Start and Restart, and what each has cost, and the tasks you sent with their own cost. Or ask in the chat ("how is my stock watcher doing?", "stop it"): Vythea reads them without asking and asks before it stops or starts one.

What it costs

WhatPrice
Compute (tasks, workers, awake apps)about $6 per GB a month, charged by the second
The models a task usesas any hosted request, on the models page
A 256 MB service online all monthabout $1.50

Every charge is under Cloud on the usage page.

What is not allowed

Mining, flooding other machines, and anything the terms forbid. An abuse guard watches every container: a miner or a flood is stopped at once, and the team is told of anything else that looks wrong. Only web traffic reaches the cloud, so game servers and other open ports are not possible yet.

Your data there

A conversation's folder and what Vythea keeps for it stay on Vythea's servers while you use them, and are deleted after 14 days without use, unless a worker in it is still running. Support can read a task and its answer only if you allow it, and every look is logged.

cloud/services.html:
Cloud and teams/Vythea Cloud

Services

Keep a bot, a scheduler or a webhook receiver running in Vythea Cloud, day and night.

A service (a worker) is a program Vythea leaves running in the cloud after a task: a Discord or Telegram bot, a scheduler, a webhook receiver. It keeps running with your computer off.

Asking for one

Say what it should do, and say to keep it running:

Watch my shop's stock every hour, email me when anything runs low, and keep it running.

Vythea builds it and tests it in the cloud, then leaves it running. Say "keep it running" or "keep it online" only when you want that: any other task runs once and stops.

Keys it needs

A service often needs a key, such as a bot's token or an API key. Give it to Vythea in the chat; it goes in /work/.env in the service's folder, not in its code.

How it keeps running

  • If it stops, it is started again.
  • If it crashes five times in ten minutes, it is stopped for good, with the reason. Read it in its output, fix it in the chat, and start it again.
  • It gets 256 MB of memory unless it needs more, from 128 to 512 MB.
  • An account may keep three running at once.
  • It is billed by the hour from your credit, and stopped if the credit runs out. See Costs.

Changing it

Ask in the chat, as you would for any change: "make the stock watcher check every half hour". Vythea changes it on the same thread, and the new code is what runs next.

Checking on it, stopping it

Ask in the chat ("how is my stock watcher doing?", "stop it"), use the Cloud page, or the terminal. See Looking after them.

A stopped service is not billed. Starting it again bills it again while it runs.

cloud/tasks.html:
Cloud and teams/Vythea Cloud

Tasks in the cloud

Send a task to Vythea Cloud from the chat or the terminal, follow it, carry it on and stop it.

A task is one piece of work Vythea does on Vythea's servers and then brings the answer back. It needs Pro, and is paid from your credit: see Costs.

When Vythea uses the cloud

Vythea picks where to build what you ask, in this order:

  1. A page, chart, document or small app that one file can hold is written on your computer, for you to preview.
  2. Anything else is built on your computer, in the project, with its own tools.
  3. Only when your computer cannot, it goes to the cloud: a tool it needs is missing and cannot be installed, the work needs more memory or time than this machine has, or you asked for the cloud.

Vythea asks before each task it sends, since it spends credit, and says in its answer that the work ran in the cloud.

Sending one from the chat

Ask in the window or the terminal: "run this in the cloud", or "build this in the cloud and tell me what failed".

The cloud sees nothing of your computer or of the conversation, so the task carries everything it needs. Vythea gives it one of these to work in:

  • Your project folder. Vythea packs the folder and sends it: every file your .gitignore keeps, hidden ones such as .env included, but never .git. This works for a private repository, or one that is only on your computer.
  • A git repository, cloned first. It must be a public https address: the cloud has no git sign-in.
  • Nothing, for work that needs no files.

Sending one from the terminal

vythea cloud "add a test for parse" --repo https://github.com/me/app

Vythea starts the task, prints each step as it goes, and then prints the answer. Options:

OptionDoes
--repo <https-url>a git repository to work in, cloned first
--branch <name>the branch to clone
--tier <tier>light (512 MB), normal (1 GB) or heavy (2 GB); light unless set
--model <name>a hosted model from the models page; the cloud's default unless set
--thread <id>carry on an earlier task's thread
--no-waitstart it, print its id and return

Sizes

Each task runs in a container of its own. Its size sets its memory and how long it may run:

TierMemoryLongest run
light512 MB15 minutes
normal1 GB30 minutes
heavy2 GB1 hour

Use heavy for big builds.

Following it

Its progress shows as it goes: in the chat, the step under way; in the terminal, each step on its own line. Closing the app or the laptop does not stop it.

vythea cloud list
vythea cloud show run_abc123

list shows your twenty most recent tasks, with how each stands, its tier and how long it ran. show prints one task's answer, or how it stands. A task is queued, running, done, failed or stopped.

The Cloud page lists them too, with what each cost.

Threads

Every task belongs to a thread: its folder and its conversation, kept on the server between tasks. To carry on where one left off, send the next task on the same thread:

vythea cloud "now make the tests pass" --thread <id>

The thread's id is printed under each answer. A thread unused for 14 days is deleted, unless a service in it is still running.

What it made

When a task makes a page or a picture, its answer ends with a link: "See what it made". It is a private live link to the thread's folder, served as it is, for you alone. Nothing runs to serve it, so it costs nothing while nobody looks. To keep a web app running for others, see Web apps.

Stopping it

vythea cloud stop run_abc123

Stop works on a task that is queued or running. Stop on the Cloud page does the same.

Letting support read it

Support cannot read a task unless you allow it, one task at a time. Every look is logged.

vythea cloud support run_abc123 on
vythea cloud support run_abc123 off

Have Vythea Cloud answer your Telegram chat when this computer is off.

cloud/web-apps.html:
Cloud and teams/Vythea Cloud

Web apps with a link

A web app Vythea builds in the cloud stays up at its own address, wakes on a visit and sleeps when nobody comes.

A web app Vythea builds in Vythea Cloud can stay up at an address of its own, for anyone with the link. Any server works: a Next.js site, a Rust API, anything that answers on a port.

Asking for one

Ask for the app and say to keep it up: "build a booking page for my studio and keep it online". Vythea builds it and tests it in the cloud, then gives you its address:

https://lc-<id>.vythea.si

Awake and asleep

  • An app wakes on the first visit. That visit waits while it starts.
  • It sleeps after ten minutes without a visit.
  • It may be awake eight hours a day. Past that, a visitor is told it wakes again tomorrow.
  • You pay only while it is awake, by the second. See Costs.
  • Awake, it gets 512 MB unless it needs more, from 256 MB to 2 GB.

Its folder stays while it sleeps, so it wakes as it was. An app can stream to its visitors (server-sent events) for as long as they stay.

A live link is not a web app

A task that makes a page gives a private live link to it ("See what it made"): the thread's files, served as they are, for you alone, with nothing running. A web app is a program that runs, at a public address. See Tasks.

What a web app cannot do yet

Only web traffic reaches the cloud: an app answers on its address over HTTPS, and other ports are not open. The address is always on vythea.si.

Looking after it

The Cloud page shows each app with its address, its state (Running, Starting, Asleep until visited, Stopped), what it printed and what it cost. See Looking after them.

data-and-privacy.html:
Account and data

Your data

What Vythea keeps on your computer, what it sends where, and adding tools from MCP servers.

Vythea keeps its data in one folder on your computer:

  • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Vythea\
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Vythea/
  • Linux: ~/.local/share/Vythea/
FileHolds
chats.json and the sessionsyour conversations, and the gateway and model picked
keys.jsonAPI keys per gateway, in plain text on your disk only
account.jsonthe Vythea sign-in for this computer
SOUL.mdwho Vythea is, in your words (optional)
USER.md, MEMORY.mdwhat it knows about you, and its own notes; edit them any time
mcp.jsonMCP servers whose tools it may use (optional)
media/images, speech and video made with no project attached

On macOS and Windows, keys and tokens are moved from that file into the Keychain or Credential Manager. The model never sees your keys, and its file tools cannot read the data folder.

With a project folder attached, its AGENTS.md is read as the project's instructions. Chat text goes to the gateway you picked and nowhere else; with the Vythea gateway, that is api.vythea.ai, which records each request's model and cost for your usage page. A task you send to Vythea Cloud runs on Vythea's servers, with only what the task itself carries.

Tools from MCP servers

List MCP servers that run as a local command in mcp.json, in the same shape Claude Desktop and Cursor use:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "everything": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"],
      "autoApprove": ["echo"]
    }
  }
}

Their tools appear once the servers answer. Every call asks first unless the tool is in autoApprove; "disabled": true leaves a server off.

developers/building-on-vythea.html:
Developers/Developers

Building on Vythea

Which way into Vythea fits your program, and what each one gives it.

Each way in is a process your program starts and talks to on stdin and stdout. Vythea's approvals, rules and hooks apply to all of them, as they do in the terminal.

Pick one

  • Your program wants an answer. Use vythea -p. It runs one task in the project folder and prints the result, as text or JSON.
  • Your program is an editor. Use vythea acp. The editor shows the turn as it runs and answers the approvals itself.
  • Your program is another agent. Use vythea mcp serve. It keeps its own model and loop, and calls Vythea's tools when it needs them.

From a script

vythea -p never stops to ask, so choose a mode that allows what the task needs. For an answer your program can parse, ask for JSON:

vythea -p --output json "how many files are in this folder?"

To get the answer itself in a shape you choose, give it a JSON Schema. The answer is printed alone, or as value with --output json:

vythea -p --json-schema schema.json "list the TODOs in src"

To keep one run going and send it more messages, use --input-format stream-json. Every option is on Scripts and one-shot runs.

From an editor

The editor starts this command and speaks the Agent Client Protocol to it:

vythea acp

Each prompt runs as an ordinary Vythea session, in the same list as the others. A call that needs a yes goes to the editor with the terminal's answers: once, always in this session, or no. Every mode but Auto is offered. See Zed and JetBrains.

From another agent

Add this command to the other agent as an MCP server:

vythea mcp serve

It offers these tools:

ToolDoes
web_fetchreads a web page
browse, use_pageopen and work a page in Vythea's browser
search_websearches the web
make_image, speak, transcribe, make_videomake and read media on the hosted models

Calls are answered one at a time, in order; start a second server to run more at once. A tool that needs a yes is refused unless the server was started with --yes, and your deny and ask rules still refuse with it. --allow-turn adds vythea_turn, which runs a whole Vythea turn on a prompt and returns its answer.

The media tools spend your credit: see Hosted models and credit.

Where Vythea gets its models: your Vythea account, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server.

getting-started.html:
Getting started

Getting started

Make an account, install Vythea, sign it in and ask it something.

Vythea is an AI agent that stays open beside your work: a window, and the same agent in a terminal. It reads and writes files, runs commands (asking first), keeps notes about you on your disk, and talks to whichever models you choose.

1. Make an account

Sign up on vythea.ai. While Vythea is in alpha, downloads come with an account; it also carries your credit for hosted models, your plan and your teams.

2. Install it

Open Download in the dashboard. It offers your own system first:

  • macOS (13 or later, Apple silicon): copy the one-line command and paste it into Terminal. It puts in the window and the terminal and opens Vythea, with no warning to click through. Or open the .dmg and drag Vythea into Applications; the first time, macOS may say it cannot verify Vythea: close the message, open System Settings › Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway next to Vythea and confirm. You only do this once.
  • Windows (11, x64): download the .zip, unpack it and run vythea.exe setup — or copy the one-line command and paste it into PowerShell, which does both.
  • Linux (x64, glibc 2.31 or later): download the .tar.gz, unpack it and run ./vythea setup — or paste the one-line command into a terminal.

Nothing needs administrator rights, and nothing goes outside your own account on the computer except, on a Mac, the app in Applications.

3. Set it up

vythea setup asks what to call you, signs you in, picks a gateway and a model, and puts the window, the terminal or both where you choose. Run it again any time to change the answers. On Windows and Linux the app then shows up in the start menu or application menu.

4. Sign it in

Signing in happens on vythea.ai: the app opens it for you, or run /login in the terminal. The computer then shows under Devices.

5. Ask it something

Type a message. Vythea answers with the model you picked, and asks before it runs a command or changes a file. Hosted models are paid from your credit; to use your own API keys instead, see Gateways.

Using Vythea

Hosted models and credit

Vythea's own models: how credit works, what Pro changes, and making images, speech and video.

Signed in, the Vythea gateway gives you chat models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and others with no key to paste. Each request is paid from your credit at the price on the models page.

Credit and plans

  • Credit is bought from $1, never runs out on a date, and works on every plan. A request is refused, with a message saying so, once it has run out; your own keys keep working.
  • Pro ($20 a month, or $199.20 a year) adds $20 of credit a month, or $240 at once on the yearly plan, charges less for every hosted model, and allows three times the requests a minute.
  • Team puts one credit pool behind a group: see Teams.
  • Each computer and each account has a per-minute limit on requests, well above normal use; past it, Vythea says how long to wait.

The usage page shows what you spent on text, media and Vythea Cloud, thirty days day by day, each model's published price beside what you paid, and how much that saved.

Using Vythea/Local models

Working offline

What Vythea can and cannot do with no internet connection.

With a local model, the agent runs with no internet at all.

Works offlineNeeds the internet
chatting with a model on this computer or your networkthe Vythea gateway and other hosted models

When the connection drops

Once a request to the web cannot connect, web search and fetching say at once that they are unavailable for now, naming the host and why, rather than each waiting to fail. They try again after two minutes in a session you are watching, or as soon as a request gets through.

A hosted model fails, saying why in the chat. Pick a local model from the menu and carry on in the same session. To keep going on its own, name a local model with /fallback.

Before you go offline

  • Download the models you will want while you still have a connection.

  • Check the setup without the network:

local-models/ollama.html:
Using Vythea/Local models

Ollama

Using a model you run with Ollama: install, pull a model, pick it in Vythea.

Ollama runs open models on your computer. Vythea looks for it at http://localhost:11434/v1 and lists its models with no setup: no key, no address to type.

Set it up

  1. Install Ollama from ollama.com and start it.

  2. Download a model that can call tools, for example:

    ollama pull qwen3:8b

  3. Pick the model from the model menu. Its models are listed under Ollama, beside your other gateways.

On first launch, choose On this computer on the setup page; its Local model row says "Detected" with the number of models once Ollama answers, or "Not found" until it does. In the terminal, the same choice is in vythea setup, and /gateways shows Ollama among the rest.

When it does not answer

local-models/overview.html:
Using Vythea

Local models

Running a model on your own computer: why you might, and what you need.

Vythea can use a model running on your own computer instead of one in the cloud. Your messages, files and tool results then never leave the machine, nothing is paid per request, and the agent keeps working with no internet.

The trade is quality and speed. A model small enough for a laptop is well behind the hosted ones at long, many-step work, and it answers only as fast as your hardware lets it.

What you need

  • A server that runs the model. Vythea does not run models itself; it talks to a server on your computer over the same OpenAI-compatible API it uses for every gateway. Ollama is found by itself; LM Studio, llama.cpp and others are added by their address.
  • A model that fits. Memory is what decides: see Choosing a model.
  • One that can call tools. The agent reads, writes and runs things through tool calls. A model made only for chat can talk, but not act.

No account and no key are needed for a local model.

In this section

  • Ollama: the quickest way to start
  • Other local servers: LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and anything OpenAI-compatible
  • Choosing a model: what fits your memory, and the context window
  • Working offline: what still works with no internet
  • Serving your accounts to other tools: the Local endpoint

The phone app runs small models on the device itself: see Mobile models.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.description: Giving Vythea more tools from MCP servers: adding them, signing in, and choosing which tools it may use.
mcp.html:
Connect and extend

MCP servers

Giving Vythea more tools from MCP servers: adding them, signing in, and choosing which tools it may use.

An MCP server gives Vythea tools of its own: a database, an issue tracker, your notes. Vythea reaches servers that run as a command on your computer, and servers reached by URL. They are listed in mcp.json in your data folder, in the same shape Claude Desktop and Cursor use, so you can copy a list across.

Adding a server

From the terminal:

vythea mcp add files -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem ~/notes
vythea mcp add github -e GITHUB_TOKEN=... -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github
vythea mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp
Option for addDoes
-t, --transport <kind>stdio (a command run here) or http; a URL means http
-e, --env <KEY=value>an environment variable for the command
-H, --header <"K: v">a header sent to a server reached by URL
--client-id <id>the app id a server that registers no apps gave you
--callback-port <port>the port that app id was registered with
CommandDoes
vythea mcp listevery server, started to see it answer
vythea mcp get <name>one server in full
vythea mcp remove <name>take one out
vythea mcp login <name>sign in to a server reached by URL, in the browser
vythea mcp logout <name>forget that sign-in

In the window, the MCP tab on the Capabilities page lists the servers, with a switch for each tool.

Writing mcp.json yourself

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "everything": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"],
      "autoApprove": ["echo"]
    },
    "hosted": {
      "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${HOSTED_KEY}" },
      "excludeTools": ["delete_*"]
    }
  }
}
  • Every call asks first, unless the tool is in autoApprove. "autoApprove": "readOnly" trusts the server's own word on which tools only read.
  • includeTools and excludeTools choose which tools Vythea sees.
  • Any text can use ${VAR}, or ${VAR:-default} for a value when the variable is not set.
  • "disabled": true leaves a server off.
  • cwd sets the folder a command runs in, and timeout_ms and startup_timeout_ms how long Vythea waits.

Servers reached by URL use streamable HTTP; the older SSE transport is not supported. Servers restart when they stop, and the list is read again when mcp.json changes.

In a session

/mcp
/mcp reload
/mcp reconnect github

/mcp shows the servers and how each is doing. It also takes enable, disable, login, logout and log (what a server printed). A server's prompts run as slash commands, and its resources can be read.

When servers bring many tools, Vythea looks them up when needed instead of sending all of them with every request.

Vythea as an MCP server

Another agent can use Vythea's media and search tools over MCP:

vythea mcp serve

--yes runs tools that need a yes without one, and --allow-turn also offers a whole Vythea turn as a tool.

Chats

Starting chats, finding them again, and what holding a message or a chat does.

Starting a chat

Type in Ask Vythea anything and tap Send. Tap Stop to stop an answer. The first message names the chat.

New chat is at the top of the screen and in the chats list.

An answer keeps going when you move to another chat. The chats list shows a moving mark beside a chat that is still answering. If an answer was cut off while the app was closed, it is asked again when you come back.

The chats list

Swipe to the right anywhere on the chat to open the list. Chats are grouped as Pinned, Today, Yesterday, This week and Earlier. Search finds a chat by its name.

Hold a chat in the list for:

ChoiceDoes

Renamegives it your own name
Name it againlets Vythea name it again from what was said
Deletedeletes it; Undo brings it back for a moment

Holding a message

Hold any message for:

ChoiceDoes

Select textopens the message so you can pick any part of it
Shareopens the phone's share sheet
Editedits your own message and asks again
Retryasks for that answer again
Retry in a forkasks again in a new chat; the original keeps what came after
Fork from herecopies the chat up to here into a new chat, named "(fork)"
Rewind to hereremoves what came after; Undo brings it back

Each answer shows how many tokens went in and came out.

Voice input

Tap the microphone in the composer and speak. The first time, allow the microphone and speech recognition.

By default your words are transcribed by ElevenLabs Scribe on Vythea, from your credit. The phone transcribes instead, for free, when Vythea cannot be reached or your account has no credit. To always use the phone, see Settings.

mobile/code-sessions.html:
Using Vythea/The mobile app

Code sessions

Changing a GitHub repo from the phone: each message runs in Vythea Cloud and opens a pull request.

On the Code side, a session works on a GitHub repo. Each message runs in Vythea Cloud, on a branch of its own, which Vythea pushes and opens as a pull request. Nothing is pushed to your main branch.

Connecting GitHub

  1. Open Settings > GitHub.
  2. Choose Connect GitHub, and install the Vythea app on GitHub, on the repos you choose.
  3. The repos show under Your repos. To add more, choose Choose repos on GitHub.

If the repo belongs to an organization, an owner has to approve the Vythea app first.

Vythea pushes only the session's own branch. Protect your main branch on GitHub as well: that is what really keeps it safe.

Starting a session

  1. Open the chats, choose Code, then New session.
  2. Choose a repository.
  3. Describe a change, and send it.

The chat shows the run starting, waiting for a container, then working. Reply with Ask for more to carry on in the same branch.

Steps

An answer lists what the run did, such as "Ran 3 commands, edited 2 files". Tap it to open Steps: each command with its output, each file with its changes, and each tool used. A step that failed is marked.

Vythea as co-author

With Vythea as co-author on, in Settings > GitHub, a session's commits end with "Co-authored-by: Vythea", and its pull request with Vythea's mark. Off, they are yours alone. This holds wherever the session starts, on the phone or a computer.

Disconnecting

Disconnect GitHub makes Vythea forget the link; sessions can no longer push. To take the app off your repos, uninstall it on GitHub.

mobile/offline.html:
Using Vythea/The mobile app

Working offline

Chatting with no internet on an iPhone: Apple Intelligence and models you download to the phone.

On an iPhone, chat can answer with no internet, from a model that runs on the phone's own chip. What you type and the photos you send stay on the phone. This is on iPhone only.

With no internet, a bar says "You are offline. Chats on this phone still open." If an answer cannot reach Vythea, it is written on the phone instead, and says which model answered.

The models

Open Settings > On this iPhone > Models, or Manage in the model menu.

ModelNotes
Apple Intelligencebuilt into iOS, no download; turn it on in the iPhone's Settings
Ternary Bonsai 2 · 4Bdownload
Ternary Bonsai 2 · 2Bdownload
Qwen3.5 2Bdownload
Qwen3.5 4Bdownload

The screen shows each model's size and what is free on the phone. Bigger models answer better, but take more space and battery. A model too big for your iPhone's memory says so before it downloads.

Downloading one

  1. Tap Get beside a model.
  2. Read the size, and tap Get again. Wi-Fi is best; the app warns you on mobile data.
  3. Keep chatting while it downloads.

Tap a model for more: Pause download, Resume download, Cancel download, Use in chat, Delete from iPhone and View on Hugging Face. To add other models, see Adding a model.

Photos

The downloaded models read text at first. To let one read photos, choose Add photo reading on it: a second download, a few hundred MB. Photos are read on the phone and stay on it. Apple Intelligence reads text only.

Web search

With internet, Ternary Bonsai 2 · 4B and Qwen3.5 can search the web through Vythea. Only the search words leave the phone.

Limits

A chat that grows too long for a model on the phone says "This chat is too long for a model on the phone. Start a new chat." If a model will not load for lack of memory, close some apps or pick a smaller one.

mobile/your-computer.html:
Using Vythea/The mobile app

Your computer

Pairing the phone with Vythea on your computer, chatting with it, and managing its accounts.

You can use Vythea on your own computer from the phone. The chat runs on the computer, with its models and tools, and the phone shows it. What you send is encrypted end to end, so Vythea's servers cannot read it.

Pairing

  1. On your computer, open Vythea, then Messaging, then Vythea app, and choose Pair a phone. It shows a code.
  2. On the phone, open Settings > Pair with a computer, and allow the camera.
  3. Scan the code.
  4. Check that the computer shows the same six digits as the phone, then choose Pair on the computer.

If your computer and phone are on the same Tailscale tailnet, the phone reaches the computer straight over it.

Chatting on your computer

In the composer, choose Computer under Where it runs. The computer's name shows where the model's name would.

When Vythea on the computer wants to do something that asks first, the phone asks "Allow on" the computer: choose Allow or Deny. See Asking first and modes.

A chat on your computer stays on it. To use Vythea Cloud, start a new chat.

If the phone cannot reach it, check that Vythea is open on the computer, with Vythea app switched on under Messaging.

Accounts on the computer

Tap a computer in Settings > Computers to see Accounts on this computer: your ChatGPT and Claude plans and your API keys. They live on the computer, in its vault. The phone adds and checks them over the encrypted link; it never keeps a key.

Each plan shows how much is left, or Limit reached and when it resets. Check now asks again.

To add one, choose Add an account, pick the provider, then:

  • Plan: choose Continue, open the page, sign in, and type or paste the code it asks for.
  • API key: paste the key and choose Add to computer. The computer checks it.

A second account of the same provider needs a name, such as Work. Under Next account when one runs out, set the order Vythea uses them in when one reaches its limit. Some providers' terms do not allow using more accounts to get past a plan's limits.

Tap an account for Use first, Sign out on this computer or Remove from this computer. The computer has to be on to add an account.

Forgetting a computer

Choose Forget this computer. The phone stops reaching it. Remove the phone on the computer too, under Messaging.

plugins.html:
Connect and extend

Plugins, hooks and more

Project instructions, plugins, hooks, language servers, and running Vythea inside Zed or JetBrains.

These files live in your data folder. A project can bring its own instructions, skills and commands, but never servers, plugins or hooks: those are programs, and whoever wrote a repository may not be the person running it.

Project instructions

AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) in a project is read as that project's instructions. Vythea reads it from the project folder and every folder above it, up to the root of the repository, and a subfolder's own when it works there.

  • AGENTS.local.md is read after it, for your own rules kept out of git.
  • A line with @path pulls in another file.
  • /init has the model write a first AGENTS.md, or fill in the one there is.
/init

Plugins

A plugin is a git repository with a plugin.json. It can bring skills, slash commands, reply styles, MCP servers and model providers.

/plugins

/plugins adds plugins from git, switches them on or off, updates and removes them, and browses marketplaces. In the window, use the Plugins page.

Every plugin is checked before it is installed. Its MCP servers and providers are used only after you allow them, and you are asked again when an update changes them.

Hooks

A hook is a command of your own that runs when something happens: before or after a tool call, at the end of a turn, or when an approval waits. List them in hooks.json, in the same shape as Claude Code's hooks, so existing scripts carry over.

  • A hook reads JSON on stdin.
  • Exit code 2 blocks the action, with what it printed to stderr as the reason.
  • A hook can block an action or keep a turn going. It can never allow something the approvals stopped.

Language servers

lsp.json lists language servers that check the files Vythea edits. Errors an edit brings in reach the model, so it can fix them without a build.

{
  "servers": {
    "rust": {
      "command": "rust-analyzer",
      "extensions": ["rs"],
      "projects": ["/home/me/code/my-app"]
    }
  }
}

Each server runs only for the projects listed. Most language servers run the project's code, so list only projects you would build yourself. A server stops after ten minutes with nothing to do.

Zed and JetBrains

Zed and JetBrains editors can run Vythea as their agent, over the Agent Client Protocol. Point the editor at this command:

vythea acp

The editor can pick the model and the mode, and reopen Vythea sessions.

Cloud and teams

Teams

One credit pool for 2 to 5 people: seats, spending limits, the audit log, and who pays.

A team shares one credit pool: everyone's hosted models draw from it. Make one on the Team page, start the Team plan, and invite people there.

Seats

  • Team is $18 a seat a month ($183.60 a year), from 2 to 5 seats, and each seat adds its value to the pool.
  • Every member uses a seat; add a seat before inviting someone past them. A seat added mid-term is charged as shown when you add it, and the pool gets the matching credit.
  • An admin can remove a seat from the next renewal: the seats paid for stay until then, and nothing is refunded.

Admins

  • Set a monthly spending limit per member; they stop at it until the next month or a higher limit.
  • Add credit to the pool any time, from $1.
  • The audit log lists every change: who joined or left, roles, limits, seats, the plan and credit.
  • Someone removed from the team stops using its pool at once.

Who pays

Each computer picks whether hosted models are paid by you or by a team you are in: /team in the terminal, or Settings > Account in the app.

Using Vythea/The terminal

Keys in the terminal

Typing, editing, history, copying and stopping in the terminal.

? on an empty line shows the keys over the box until the next key. /help lists them too, with the ones that work in your terminal.

Sending and new lines

KeyDoes
Entersend
\ then Enter, or Ctrl+Ja new line
Shift+Entera new line, in terminals that can tell it from Enter
Ctrl+Gopen what is in the box in your editor ($VISUAL, then $EDITOR); closing it puts the text back

You can type while Vythea works: what you send reaches the model at the reply's next step, and shows as queued until then.

Editing the line

KeyDoes
Option+arrows, or Alt+B and Alt+Fmove a word
Alt+D, Alt+Backspacedelete a word
Ctrl+U, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Wcut to the start, to the end, or a word
Ctrl+Yput back what was last cut
Ctrl+_undo the last change to the line

History

What you send is kept for each project folder across sessions, so ↑ reaches yesterday's prompts.

KeyDoes
↑ and ↓, or Ctrl+P and Ctrl+Nstep through what you sent before
Ctrl+Rsearch what you sent, newest first, narrowed as you type

Answers to questions, such as a key, are never kept, nor is anything typed in a private chat. The history is prompt-history.jsonl in your data folder; delete it to forget it.

Modes and stopping

KeyDoes
Shift+Tab, or Alt+Mstep through the modes
Escstop a reply; turn down a card or a list; clear the line
Esc twice on an empty boxgo back to an earlier message
Ctrl+Cstop a reply and stay; clear what is typed
Ctrl+C twice on an empty box, or Ctrl+Dleave

A line cleared with Esc comes back with ↑. When you leave, Vythea says which session it was and how to come back to it.

Output and the screen

KeyDoes
Ctrl+O, or a clickshow all of a tool's output, or fold it again
Ctrl+Lclear the screen
Endgo back to the bottom after scrolling up
Ctrl+Vattach the picture on the clipboard

Selecting text with the mouse copies it. /copy copies the last reply as written.

Running a command yourself

A line starting with ! runs as a command in the session's folder, without asking, since you typed it. The model sees what it printed with your next message.

terminal/scripts.html:
Using Vythea/The terminal

Scripts and one-shot runs

vythea -p: asking once from a script, its options, JSON output and running with nothing set up.

vythea -p asks one question, prints the answer and exits. Nobody watches such a run, so it never waits on a question: it decides from the task and the project folder.

vythea -p "list the TODOs in src and say which are urgent"

In the default mode, a -p run cannot write files or run commands, and warns you of it. Choose a mode that allows what it needs:

vythea -p --mode accept-edits "fix the failing test"

See Asking first and modes.

Options

OptionDoes
--output <form>text (the answer), json, or stream-json
--max-rounds <n>tool rounds a message gets before it stops (100)
--model <name>use this model instead of the one set up
--tools <a,b>only these tools, by name
--budget <tokens>stop once this many tokens are spent, over every message the run is sent
--input-format <form>text (the question), or stream-json: messages, interrupts and answers as JSON lines on stdin
--permission-prompt-tool stdiowith stream-json in, ask stdin about each call that needs a yes
--json-schema <file>answer in JSON this schema checks; the schema itself can stand in for the file
--dump-configprint the settings and limits a -p run with the same flags gets, as JSON, without running

--json-schema needs a new session, so it does not go with -c, -r or stream-json in.

JSON output

--output json prints one JSON object with the answer and what it took: the session, the model, the cost, and how many calls were refused. --output stream-json prints a JSON line each time the run moves on, then that object as the last line.

vythea -p --output json "how many files are in this folder?"

A time limit

VYTHEA_DEADLINE gives the run a number of seconds. At 80% of it, the run is told to write its outputs; at the end it stops, with a result whose status is deadline.

VYTHEA_DEADLINE=600 vythea -p --mode bypass "build the report"

Running with nothing set up

In a container or on a fresh machine, a -p run can take its server from the environment, saving none of it:

VariableDoes
AGENT_BASE_URLask this OpenAI-compatible server instead of the gateway set up
AGENT_API_KEYthe key to send it
AGENT_MODELthe model to ask, unless --model names one
AGENT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 AGENT_MODEL=llama3.2 vythea -p "hello"

terminal/slash-commands.html:
Using Vythea/The terminal

Every slash command

All of the terminal's slash commands, grouped by what they do.

Type / in a conversation to see these, narrowed as you type. /help <command> says more about one. Skills, MCP prompts and your own commands are offered as you type their names too.

Sessions

CommandDoes
/newstart a fresh session
/resumepick up a session; a word finds it by title or by what was said
/renamename this session, or have a model name it
/branchcarry on in a copy of this session
/rewindgo back to any message: restore the chat, the code, or both
/undothe same as /rewind
/retryask your last message again
/compactsummarise earlier turns now; a number keeps that many last turns
/contextwhat fills the context, part by part, and how full it is
/btwask something aside; the answer is not kept
/copycopy the last reply as written; /copy 2 the one before it
/exportwrite the conversation as Markdown: /export [file]
/statusversion, session, folder, model, mode, account and context
/diffwhat changed in the project; /diff session for this session's files
/whereshow the project folder and session file
/importcontinue a session from Claude Code or Codex
/retentiondelete sessions older than a number of days, or off to keep them
/clearstart fresh in a new session; the last one stays in /resume

Model

CommandDoes
/modelshow or change the model; add image, speech or video for those, side for summaries, or names for session names
/efforthow hard the model should think
/thinkingshow the model's thinking, or hide it
/stylelist reply styles, or pick one: /style concise
/fallbackmodels to carry on with when yours is overloaded or out of credit
/voiceread replies aloud as they stream, paid from your credit

Modes

CommandDoes
/modeshow or change how much runs without asking
/planread and search only, never change files; /plan on or off
/decisionswhat auto mode's judge let run or blocked in this session
/verifyask the model to build or test after it changes files, or not

Tools

CommandDoes
/searchlet the model search the web; /search services for your own, /search keyless for DuckDuckGo
/imageattach a picture to your next message: /image <path>
/previewserve an HTML or SVG file to your browser: /preview [--open] <path>
/skillsskills: use one, switch them on or off, add from GitHub
/mcpMCP servers and their prompts
/pluginsplugins: add from git, switch on or off, allow servers, update, remove
/inithave the model write or fill in the project's AGENTS.md

Memory

CommandDoes
/memorywhat is kept between sessions; /memory edit, log or restore
/rememberwhen this chat saves memory and where; /remember <text> keeps that
/memory-reviewlook back now and then for what to remember, or stop; only while saving on its own

Background work

CommandDoes
/jobscommands still running in the background
/looprun a prompt every so often, or at the model's pace; /loop stop ends it
/heartbeatlook in on this session every so many minutes
/goalkeep working until a goal is met: /goal <text>, --check <command>, resume, clear
/agentshelpers working for this session; stop one or tell it something
/workflowsworkflow runs: look in, pause, stop, resume, skip or retry
/crewlet Vythea run workflows of helpers for big tasks
/notifysay when a reply ends or needs you while you are away, or stop

Account

CommandDoes
/connectconnect or sign in to providers, add gateways of your own, see plan and usage
/teambill hosted models to a team or to yourself
/loginsign in to Vythea
/logoutsign out on this machine
/whoamiwho is signed in
/walletthe wallet the agent pays from: balances, limits, x402, networks, history
/usagetokens and cost: this session, by day and by model
/insightsthe last weeks by day and hour, top tools and models: /insights 8

Help and leaving

CommandDoes
/helpwhat Vythea can do here
/exitleave

To send a message that starts with a slash as words, start it with //.

troubleshooting.description: Checking the setup with vythea doctor, what common errors mean, and where the logs are.
troubleshooting.html:
Help

Troubleshooting

Checking the setup with vythea doctor, what common errors mean, and where the logs are.

Check the setup

vythea doctor

It checks the version, your system, the data folder and the space left on its disk, the settings, where your keys are kept, the logs, the last crash, and whether the gateway answers. It ends with "No problems found." or says what is wrong. To check without using the network:

vythea doctor --offline

When a message fails

A failed request says why in the chat, and in the window offers the fix. The usual reasons:

It saysWhat to do
the key was refusedcheck the key under Settings > Accounts, or with /connect
out of creditadd credit on Billing, switch to a gateway with your own key, or set a fallback model
a rate limitwait the time it names; Vythea waits out short limits by itself
the provider is busytry again, or pick another model
the conversation is too long/compact summarises earlier turns; /new starts fresh

/fallback names models to carry on with when yours is overloaded or out of credit:

/fallback

Signing in

  • If the browser does not open, the app offers to open the page again or copy its link.
  • /whoami shows who is signed in on this computer; /login signs in again.
  • Devices lists the computers signed in to your account.

A model on your own server answers badly

If Vythea does not know a model's limits, set them in the environment:

VYTHEA_CONTEXT_WINDOW=32000 VYTHEA_MAX_OUTPUT=4096 vythea

context_window and max_output in settings.json do the same for good.

Logs and crashes

Vythea keeps a log in logs/ and crash reports in crashes/, in your data folder. They stay on your computer. vythea doctor shows where they are and the last crash.

Starting over

Run setup again to change your name, gateway, model or what is installed:

vythea setup

Uninstalling keeps your data folder, so your sessions and memory stay.

Still stuck

Write to support@vythea.ai with what you did, what it said, and the output of vythea doctor.

wallet.html:
Connect and extend

Wallet

The wallet the agent pays from: paying sites that ask to be paid, sending money, and the limits you set.

Vythea has a wallet of its own that the agent can pay from, within limits you set. It is separate from your credit and from the VYTH wallet on vythea.ai (see VYTH).

  • Make a new wallet, or bring one in from MetaMask, Phantom or any wallet app by its recovery phrase or key.
  • It works on Base, Ethereum, Solana and any EVM network.
  • Sites that ask to be paid (x402) are paid in USDC, within your limits: asked each time, or paid on their own below a price you choose.
  • Sending money always asks.
  • Keys stay in the system's vault. The agent never sees them.

Open the Wallet page in the window, Settings > Wallet, /wallet in a session, or vythea wallet in the terminal.

Setting it up

vythea wallet new
vythea wallet import
vythea wallet balance

new makes a wallet with a new recovery phrase; keep that phrase safe. import brings one in by its recovery phrase or a key; --index <n> picks which account under the phrase, from 0. watch <address> only follows an address's balances.

Limits

vythea wallet limits --per-payment 1 --per-day 5 --per-month 50
vythea wallet x402 ask
OptionDoes
--auto-up-to <$>the most an x402 payment costs to be paid without asking
--per-payment <$>the cap on one payment by the agent
--per-day <$>the cap on what it spends in 24 hours
--per-month <$>the cap on what it spends in 30 days

vythea wallet x402 takes off, ask or auto. The caps hold even when you say yes to a payment; what you send yourself is not counted.

To stop the agent paying at once, and to let it again:

vythea wallet pause
vythea wallet resume

More commands

CommandDoes
vythea walletwallets, rules and what was spent
vythea wallet listthe wallets and their addresses
vythea wallet historythe latest payments
vythea wallet send <amount> [token] to <address> on <network>send money yourself; asks first
vythea wallet sites allow|block|clear [site]pay only these sites, or never these
vythea wallet chainsthe networks; switch one on or off, or set its RPC
vythea wallet prefer <network>...the networks tried first when a site takes several
vythea wallet tokens add <network> <address>a token to show and send
vythea wallet save <name> <address>keep an address to send to
vythea wallet only-saved on|offthe agent sends only to saved addresses
vythea wallet default <name>the wallet that pays when none is named
vythea wallet rename <name> <new>call a wallet something else
vythea wallet reveal <name>show its recovery phrase or key
vythea wallet remove <name>take a wallet out of Vythea

A command that sends, shows a key or changes the rules runs only when you type it at a terminal, never when the agent runs it.
